Govind Prasad Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17
February, 2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Jbp:15069
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Himanshu Joshi

On The 17 th Of February, 2026
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 27894 of 2022

Govind Prasad Sharma
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Eshaan Datt - Advocate for the petitioner.
Shri C.S. Upadhyay - Panel Lawyer for respondent/State.

Order 
The present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is filed seeking quashment of the order dated 09.05.2022 passed in Criminal Revision No.52/2021 1st Additional Sessions Judge, Sehore, whereby the revision preferred by the petitioner challenging the order dated 13.09.2021 framing charges under Section 272 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 was dismissed and the order framing charges was affirmed.

entities.text: Criminal Revision No.52/2021 1st Additional Sessions Judge, Sehore
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts are that the Police Station Kotwali, Sehore registered Crime No. 779/2019 against the petitioner, Govind Prasad Sharma, son of Shri Goverdhan Sharma, for offences punishable under Section 272 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 59(1) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

As per the prosecution case, it is alleged that on 24.07.2019 at about 1:00 PM, the petitioner,
proprietor of M/s Krishna Dairy, Khajanchi Line, Sehore, was found allegedly mixing detergent in milk and paneer products at his shop.

It is further alleged that on the basis of a written complaint dated 03.09.2019 submitted by Food Inspector NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:15069 2 MCRC-27894-2022 Kumari Dipali Kange to Police Station Kotwali, Sehore, the aforesaid offences were registered against the petitioner.

entities.text: NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:15069 2 MCRC-27894-2022 Kumari Dipali Kange
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Thereafter, the First Information Report was lodged alleging that the milk was prepared by mixing detergent, which constitutes the offences mentioned above.

3. As per the report dated 24.12.2019 issued by the Referral Food Laboratory, Mysore, it is stated as under:
"Our opinion on the sample under reference is enclosed for your kind perusal.
The sample has been completely utilised for analysis and the container discarded as it was found unfit for further use."

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is respectfully submitted that the present case is squarely covered by the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramnath v. State of U.P. [2024] 2 S.C.R. 743., wherein it has been held that in circumstances where proceedings are initiated under the Food Safety and Standards Act,
2006, the provisions of Section 272 of the Indian Penal Code would not be attracted.

entities.text: Ramnath v. State of U.P. [2024] 2 S.C.R. 743
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. In view of the report dated 24.12.2019 issued by the Referral Food Laboratory, Mysore, and the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the aforesaid judgment, continuation of proceedings under Section 272 of the Indian Penal Code against the petitioner is wholly unsustainable in law.
6. Accordingly, this MCrC is partly allowed.

The impugned orders to the extent they pertain to framing of charge under Section 272 of the Indian Penal Code be quashed, and the concerned authority may proceed, in accordance with Section 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

(HIMANSHU JOSHI) JUDGE rv Govind Prasad Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95441422/
